value.rationale: Length six is a classical small deletion-code benchmark where prior work explicitly showed the optimum is nonunique but stopped at examples. Completing the optimizer census, isolating the universal core and unique perfect code, and describing the symmetry/coverage strata is a natural finite classification rather than a recomputation of \(A(6,1)\).
residual_risks: An obscure historical exhaustive census may be absent from modern indexes; targeted exact-count/core/orbit searches did not locate one.

final_claim: Among binary length-six single-deletion-correcting codes, there are exactly nine labeled maximum codes of size ten; all contain the same four-word core, exactly one is perfect and equals \(\mathrm{VT}_0(6)\), the nonperfect descendant-union sizes have the stated 26/28/30 histogram, and reversal plus global complement partitions the nine maxima into six orbits of sizes \(2,2,2,1,1,1\).
limitations: The result is only for binary length six and one deletion, and the symmetry statement is restricted to reversal and global complement.
